suggestion.problemOrOpportunity: Every decision must record a reopening condition, and 1,134 of 1,135 are prose that nothing evaluates. The one evaluable predicate names a metric the meter cannot resolve, so the meter's reopen-candidate count is zero whatever the state. Three numeric conditions had occurred at the subject commit without a recorded observation, and the previous review found another the same way.
suggestion.scope: Two bounded steps. First, make the existing evaluator honest: refuse a predicate whose metric the meter cannot resolve, and resolve budget-row metrics such as coldStartBytes.executor. Second, add a small probe table keyed by register or decision id (a command and a threshold per row) for the conditions that name a number, run it from planning entry and list the rows whose condition holds. Start with the rows measured here: plan check time, newer release tags, per-order and weekly evidence bytes, collectSources and release list times. No new gate and no refusal.
affectedUsers: the operator who deferred a decision on a stated threshold
reviewers who today find fired conditions by hand
suggestion.expectedValue: A deferral on a measurable threshold becomes self-reporting: the pass that would act on it sees it at entry. The health line's candidate count starts to carry information.
suggestion.uncertainty: About 85 of the 1,134 prose conditions look numeric by pattern match; how many can be probed in under a few seconds each is unmeasured. Whether the three observations here would change a planning decision is the operator's call.
risks: A probe table becomes one more list to keep current
Timing probes vary with host load and could report noise as a reopening
alternatives: Require the predicate form for any new condition that states a number, and leave existing prose alone
Keep hand observation and add the three fired conditions to the register in the next pass
